observed: the first rename (#2201, 8,719 moves) planned rewrites over the checked-out files only and listed a file outside the sparse checkout as absent only when its path named Synexia; Java files importing a moved package, not checked out, were never rewritten, so the commit was inconsistent
correction: every in-scope tracked file that is not checked out is ABSENT (unknown content) and apply refuses; --tree REV reads every blob through one git cat-file --batch (no lazy fetch) and apply writes one commit through git fast-import, so a sparse or partial checkout renames the whole tree
lesson: a rename over a sparse checkout renames unknown content; plan and apply from the tree

observed: read_text and write_text normalised line endings: 4 files of #2201 lost their CRLF (two intake JSON files, two Java files)

lesson: a text rewrite recipe touches only the tokens it names; bytes it does not name are kept

observed: separate PATH_RULES accepted _synexia_ after an underscore while TEXT_RULES needed a word boundary: 17 workflows still called m3/compatibility/check_synexia_*.py after those files had moved (CI: No such file or directory)

observed: synexia-m3-x became m3-m3-x in #2201 (601 text occurrences, 36 paths, M3_M3_ 25); none existed before the rename
correction: DOUBLE collapses a repeated m3-/m3_/M3-/M3_ prefix to one, and QUICK admits it

correction: lineage is detected on every suffix of a name; a colliding lineage file follows its renamed directory and keeps its name, two passes (claims, then moves); NamingScan.pathConformant mirrors the rule
lesson: two executors of one table must share its collision rule, not only its patterns

observed: #2201 CI: "source custody mismatch", "installed source mismatch", "receiver source drift"; manifests and receipts pin sha256, git blob ids and paths of the renamed files
correction: reseal.py carries every pin from before to after, round after round to a fixed point (a manifest pinned by a receipt changes one round later), writes RENAME_RESEAL.tsv, reports AMBIGUOUS values instead of guessing

observed: census of the renamed tree 7458a6cc: package com.m3.synexia.importer became jdk.m3.synexia.importer while its directory became jdk/m3/m3/importer (SEGMENT knew only slashes, DOUBLE only - and _); 11 types directly in package com.synexia (com.synexia.M3ProblemRecipePlanner) kept the old package because PKG looked ahead for a lowercase letter only

observed: the base tree also carries org.synexia.m3.recipe (4 sources, 16 references) and packages glued to a TSV or newline escape inside strings (recipe\tcom.synexia.rewrite.X, \ncom.synexia.rewrite.Y) or to an underscore (lab_com.synexia.rewrite.X); \b in the PKG rules missed all of them while SEGMENT_DOT would have renamed only the middle segment (com.m3.rewrite)

lesson: a package has more than one root and more than one boundary; the census over the base tree lists them before the rules are written

observed: the round-based reseal of rename 13a3fe71dfd stopped after 8 rounds ("a pin cycle"); each round scanned all 142,517 blobs; hash-chained history resources (each entry pins the previous one) are deeper than 8, and consistent records cannot form a cycle at all
correction: a graph pass: one scan hashes every blob into a digest index (a base digest of renamed bytes names the renamed blob, AMBIGUOUS when the old bytes still exist), one scan records which blob pins which, the blobs that must change are resealed in dependency order (Kahn), each read once; a cycle from a corrupted record terminates and is reported
lesson: a fixed point over a dependency graph is a topological order, not a loop with a cap

observed: the standalone check over every blob of rename 13a3fe71dfd left 13 N_PATH: KEEP_PATH kept the whole path of licenses/Synexia-LICENSE and Synexia-NOTICE, so 8 legal files stayed in canonical/synexia-openrewrite-recipes/ while their crates moved to m3-openrewrite-recipes/; check-synexia.py matched no rule; the full-tree JUnit run (81 s, all blobs) agreed with Python on every text line and disagreed on 4 lineage paths kept in place because their name-kept target existed

observed: the recheck reseal(tools, 9a3a01d6d3b) was not empty (1,221 files, 1,413 values): the bytes 6c42ad2a.. were at after-028.txt (in scope, renamed) and at lineage manifest.tsv copies (kept), so the digest was ambiguous in the renamed tree; the reseal then carried the moved paths inside the copies and they converged to the renamed bytes, which made the digest unambiguous one pass too late
correction: reseal_to_fixed_point repeats graph passes until one changes nothing and squashes them into one commit with the ledger; ambiguity is decided on the tree the reseal no longer changes
lesson: a decision that depends on the output (ambiguity) is taken on the fixed point, not on the input

observed: the product name had 9+ spellings (M3jdk21 94k, m3jdk21 31k, M3JDK21 8.6k, M3Jdk21* types, m3-jdk21, M3_JDK, M3 JDK, M3-JDK); the user chose per-kind JDK style; M3jdk21 and M3JDK21 in code are mostly strings, repository paths and links, where a prose rewrite would break string matches

observed: apply --tree REV --ref REF --only <dir> wrote RENAME_MAP.tsv from the scoped plan alone: #2556 (apply --only m3/tooling/module-packs/text-tools/ m3/lexicon/) left the map with its header and nothing else, dropping all 32 rows for paths outside the scope (m3/search/qualification/relocation-20261106-fastsearch/diff/stub/..., the jdk21-array-only-entry-facades rows); on master feae0743e6c, apply --only m3/nlp/ (moves=0) still dropped 32 of 32
correction: merged_map: a scoped apply owns the rows of the files it selects (selects(), the predicate plan_moves chooses paths with, and the path is in the tree); such a row takes this run's target in place or goes when the run keeps its path; every other row (outside the scope, or an earlier move whose old path is gone) stays byte for byte in its place, new moves follow, and an unchanged merge returns the old bytes; a whole-tree apply still writes its own moves; apply --only m3/nlp/ on master now writes a tree identical to master's (map diff empty)
lesson: a scoped run may rewrite only what its scope selects: a shared ledger that a scoped run writes is merged by the same path predicate that chose the files, never replaced by the scoped result
